message.content: Nxeon platform (/opt/nxeon). NxLabs is live at `nxeon.cloud/mods` with real backend data (verified Modrinth/Spiget/Thunderstore mod data, real icons/downloads/licenses, ratings/comments, search/filters). Three real visual bugs to fix, confirmed by the owner's own screenshots — investigate each properly in a real browser (Playwright) rather than guessing from code alone. ## Bug 1: The homepage hero image is invisible `app/(marketing)/mods/page.tsx` passes `` as the `visual` prop to `` (`components/marketing/primitives.tsx`). Both `/nxlabs/hero-collage.png` and `/nxlabs/logo.png` are confirmed serving correctly (HTTP 200, correct file sizes — verified via curl, so it's not a missing/404 asset). But the owner's live screenshot of this exact page shows a completely plain dark hero background with NO visible collage image at all. `PageHero` wraps the visual in `{visual && {visual}}` (`components/marketing/Reveal.tsx`) — a scroll-triggered fade-in using a real `IntersectionObserver` (not a naive CSS-only trick, so it should fire correctly even for above-the-fold content in most cases, but confirm this empirically rather than assuming). Load the real page in Playwright, screenshot it at first paint AND after a short wait, inspect the actual DOM/computed styles of the image element (is it `opacity:0`? `display:none`? zero-height due to a missing explicit dimension combined with a flex/grid parent? cropped off-screen by `lg:pl-6` positioning at a specific viewport width?). Find the REAL root cause, don't assume it's the Reveal wrapper without confirming. Per this codebase's own established design discipline: everything meant to be read/seen must be visible at page-rest without requiring a scroll interaction to trigger it — if the real cause IS a scroll-triggered reveal failing for above-the-fold content, remove the Reveal wrapper for this specific hero visual (keep Reveal for genuinely below-the-fold content elsewhere) rather than patch around the symptom. ## Bug 2: Per-game and per-mod hero art needs to be verified consistent across ALL 5 catalogued families, not just Minecraft The owner said game/mod pages "look like this" (implying a problem) but the Minecraft example he showed actually has a real, correct hero image. Check the other 4 real catalogued families — rust, valheim, cs2, palworld — on both their marketing game-listing page (`app/(marketing)/mods/games/[family]/page.tsx`) and portal equivalent (`app/dashboard/nxlabs/games/[family]/page.tsx`), and on individual mod detail pages for each family. Confirm every one resolves real, correct, game-specific hero art (reuse `gameArt()`/`GAME_ART_SLUG` from `lib/nx/catalog.ts`/`lib/games.ts`, the same source the `/game-servers` cover carousel and the `GameLandingCombined` template use) — fix any family showing a missing, wrong, or generic placeholder image. ## Bug 3: Mod cards look inconsistent and "really bad" (owner's words) — likely a real vs. fabricated art mismatch Two different mod-card visual styles exist on different pages right now, both showing the SAME real mods (e.g. Lithium, EssentialsX, WorldGuard): the per-game page (`/mods/games/minecraft`) shows clean, simple, icon-only cards — this looks authentic and matches Modrinth's actual real icon style. The cross-game homepage/browse page (`/mods`, via `components/mods/StoreBrowser.tsx`) shows the SAME mods with a much busier card design that appears to layer a generic decorative/illustrated background behind the same icon (e.g. EssentialsX's flask icon sits on top of an unrelated "candles and books" illustrated scene; Cobblemon's pokéball sits on a generic fantasy-landscape illustration) — these background illustrations do NOT look like real Modrinth screenshots or gallery images for these specific mods (recall: only 12 of 119 mods actually have real Modrinth gallery images verified so far). Investigate `components/mods/StoreBrowser.tsx` (and any card sub-component it uses) to find where this card background art comes from. If it's a fabricated/generic decorative image NOT sourced from the mod's real data (e.g. a hardcoded placeholder texture, an AI-generated stock image, or a category-level generic backdrop presented as if it were mod-specific), remove it — this violates the "real data or honest omission, never fake" discipline enforced everywhere else in this codebase this session. Replace with either: (a) the mod's REAL gallery/featured image when `galleryUrls` has one, or (b) a clean, honest icon-only treatment (matching the per-game page's simpler style) when it doesn't — do not fabricate per-mod artwork. Make the two card styles (per-game page vs. cross-game homepage) visually consistent with each other, both using this same real-data-or-clean-icon rule. ## Process - Use Playwright to actually load and screenshot: the `/mods` homepage (checking hero visibility), all 5 families' game pages (marketing + portal), and a sample of individual mod pages across families, at desktop and mobile widths, before and after your fix. - `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. - Check CLAUDE.md's build-isolation rule — don't build directly in /opt/nxeon. - Credential hygiene: DB reads via `scripts/_tmp-*.ts` importing `db` from `../lib/db`, run via `npx tsx`. Never print a raw `psql`/`DATABASE_URL` string. - Deploy: commit → push → `deploy-staging.sh` → verify 200 → `promote-production.sh` → verify 200 and a genuinely fresh BUILD_ID (record `cat /opt/nxeon/.next/BUILD_ID` first). A separate agent may be concurrently working on a bulk mod-import task in this same repo — if a deploy collides, retry once after confirming staging is healthy; if you see uncommitted changes in the working tree that aren't yours when you go to commit, do not discard them, only stage/commit your own specific files. Report back: the actual root cause of the invisible hero image (not a guess — what you confirmed via real DOM/style inspection) and the fix, confirmation all 5 families have correct hero art on every page type, exactly what was producing the fabricated-looking card backgrounds and how you fixed it, before/after screenshots, and the production deploy confirmation with fresh BUILD_ID.
